title: Saag Gosht
subtitle: Slow-braised lamb in a thick spinach and spice gravy
excerpt: Tender pieces of lamb shoulder cooked down into dark, spiced spinach. The spinach melts into the sauce and coats every piece of meat. A proper weekend curry that improves overnight.
sourceNotes: Anglo-Indian home cooking tradition. Combines Punjabi saag technique with slow-braised lamb shoulder.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze in portions for up to 3 months. Defrost fully before reheating over a low heat with a splash of water.
recipe.batchNotes: Double or triple the recipe easily. Use a large stockpot and extend the braising time by 15 minutes.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Tastes better the next day. Cool fully, refrigerate, and reheat gently on the hob.

content.text: Saag gosht is lamb braised slowly into a deep, spiced spinach sauce. The spinach breaks down completely and clings to the meat. Keep the heat low and give it time.

items.prepNote: cut into 4 cm pieces, bone-in or boneless

content.text: Heat the oil in a large saucepan over a medium-high heat. Add the cumin seeds and let them sizzle for 30 seconds.
Add the onions and cook for 12 minutes, stirring often, until deep golden brown. Do not rush this step.
Add the garlic and ginger. Cook for 2 minutes, scraping the base of the pan. Add the ground spices and cook for 1 minute more.
Add the lamb pieces and brown all over for 5 minutes. Add the yoghurt a tablespoon at a time, stirring between each addition.
Tip in the tinned tomatoes and water. Season with salt. Bring to a simmer, then cover and cook on a low heat for 45 minutes.
Add the spinach in large handfuls, stirring until each batch wilts. Cover and cook for a further 20 minutes until the lamb is tender.
Use a blender to roughly blitz the spinach sauce in the pan, or remove half and blend it. Return to the heat.
Stir in the garam masala and butter if using. Simmer for 5 minutes. Taste and adjust salt. Scatter over fresh coriander and serve.

items.symptom: The lamb is still tough after 45 minutes.
items.cause: Lamb shoulder needs longer than leaner cuts.
items.fix: Continue cooking with the lid on for 20 to 30 minutes more, adding a splash of water if it looks dry.

items.cause: The spinach released a lot of liquid.
items.fix: Remove the lid and simmer on a medium heat for 10 minutes to reduce and concentrate the sauce.

items.symptom: The yoghurt split into grainy curds.
items.cause: The heat was too high when the yoghurt was added.
items.fix: Whisk the sauce vigorously. Next time, lower the heat before adding the yoghurt one spoon at a time.
